name: claims-qa
notes: P13 V13.1: ten queries with a known answer fact. Synthetic pages only (RFC 2606 .test hosts), no personal data. Pages are listed in the order web_research reads them, so the first page is the one the shipped lead-sentence rule quotes. Cases 9 and 10 are deliberately easy for the baseline; the rest bury the fact below a plausible-sounding intro sentence, a licence banner or a table of contents.

pages.title: Configuring connections
pages.text:
The server reads its settings from postgresql.conf when it starts, and an operator can reload the file without a restart for most parameters.
The default for max_connections is 100 connections, which is enough for a small team but not for a connection pool behind an application server.

pages.title: Connection limits
pages.text:
Every backend consumes a slot, so the pool size must stay below the server limit.
A pool of twenty clients per replica is a common starting point for a read heavy workload.

pages.title: Asynchronous control flow
pages.text:
This chapter covers asynchronous control flow in Rust and the ways a future can be polled to completion.
The tokio::select! macro waits on several futures at once and runs the branch that completes first, cancelling the others.

pages.title: Waiting on multiple futures
pages.text:
Polling two futures from one task used to need a hand written state machine.
The runtime provides a combinator for the common case.

pages.title: Target domain
pages.text:
This documentation page is part of the Chrome DevTools Protocol reference and is licensed under the Apache License.
A flat session is opened with Target.attachToTarget, which returns the session id that every later command must carry.

pages.title: Sessions and targets
pages.text:
A browser target exposes every page as a separate target.
Inspect the target list before attaching to avoid an orphaned session.

pages.title: Activating a virtual environment
pages.text:
Activating a virtual environment differs between shells and operating systems, so check the table for the shell you use.
On Windows the venv puts its entry points in Scripts\activate, which you run from cmd.exe before starting Python.

pages.title: Virtual environments
pages.text:
A virtual environment keeps the interpreter and the site packages of a project apart from the system installation.
Create one per project directory.

pages.title: Status codes a client must handle
pages.text:
This section lists the status codes a client must handle and explains when each code is expected to appear.
A 429 response carries a Retry-After header that tells the client how long to wait before it sends another request.

pages.title: Rate limiting clients
pages.text:
Servers that rate limit usually return a short body explaining the policy.
The client should back off instead of retrying immediately.

pages.title: Fixture basics
pages.text:
Fixtures are functions that run before a test and provide a fixed baseline the test can rely on.
To share one fixture across the whole test module, declare it with scope="session" so it is created once.

pages.title: Sharing test setup
pages.text:
Test setup that connects to a database should not run for every function.
A wider scope keeps the connection open for the module.

pages.title: Healthchecks
pages.text:
A healthcheck tells Compose how to test whether a container is ready to serve traffic.
The interval: 30s key controls how often Compose runs that test, and the retries key bounds the failures.

pages.title: Waiting for dependencies
pages.text:
depends_on waits for the dependency container to start, not for the service inside it to answer.
Readiness requires a healthcheck on the dependency itself.

pages.title: Что такое CORS
pages.text:
CORS — это механизм, который позволяет браузеру запрашивать ресурсы с другого домена.
Сервер разрешает такой запрос заголовком Access-Control-Allow-Origin, где перечислены допустимые источники.

pages.title: Проверка запросов
pages.text:
Браузер отправляет предварительный запрос, если метод или заголовки не относятся к простым.
Ответ на него тоже должен содержать разрешающие заголовки.

pages.title: Squashing commits
pages.text:
To squash commits, start an interactive rebase and mark the commits you want to combine with squash.
The editor keeps the message of the first commit unless you rewrite it.

pages.title: Cleaning up history
pages.text:
A tidy history is easier to review than a long chain of fixup commits.
Rewrite only commits that nobody else has pulled.

pages.title: Быстрый ответ
pages.text:
Блок «Быстрый ответ» показывает короткую справку над результатами поиска.
Он появляется для фактических запросов и не заменяет список ссылок.
